# 3. Dataset

## 3(a) Loading raw data and defining one row
Peek at one row of the full person ACS 1-Year PUMS
```{r}
pums_files <- c("/Users/gracekemmerenhendricks/Documents/Autumn 26/data/csv_pus/psam_pusa.csv",
                "/Users/gracekemmerenhendricks/Documents/Autumn 26/data/csv_pus/psam_pusb.csv")

peek <- read_csv(pums_files[1], n_max = 1, show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

peek
```
One row = one person (one PUMS person record), uniquely identified by `SERIALNO` + `SPORDER`.

```{r load-data}
# OLD SELECTION OF VARS
# person_vars <- c("RT", "SERIALNO",  "SPORDER", "DIVISION", "REGION", "STATE", "ADJINC",
#                  "AGEP", "CIT", "DEAR", "DEYE", "MAR", "MIL", "MLPA", "MLPB", "MLPCD", "SEX",
#                  "SCHL", "DIS", "DRAT", "MSP", "PAOC", "PINCP", "SCIENGRLP",
#                  "RACAIAN", "RACASN", "RACBLK", "RACSOR", "RACWHT", "RACNH",
#                  "RACPI", "RAC1P", "VPSP", "PERNP", "PWGTP", "HISP")

# NEW SELECTIONF OF VARS: single race code, using PERNP, not PINCP
person_vars <- c("RT", "SERIALNO", "ADJINC", "SPORDER", "PWGTP",
                 "MIL", "VPSP",
                 "STATE", "AGEP", "SEX", "RAC1P", "MAR", "PAOC",
                 "CIT", "NATIVITY", "LANX", "ENG", "WAOB",
                 "DIS", "DRAT", "DRATX", "DEAR", "DEYE", "DPHY", "DREM", "DDRS", "DOUT",
                 "JWMNP", "WKHP", "WKWN",
                 "SCHL", "FOD1P", "SCIENGRLP",
                 "PERNP")


pums_raw <- pums_files |>
  map(~ read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_select = all_of(person_vars),
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))) |>
  list_rbind()

dim(pums_raw)

```

### Eligibility filters (definitional, NOT data-driven, so safe before the split)
Veterans who are not currently on active duty or in Reserve/National Guard Status: `MIL` code 2 
(verified in the data dictionary: 1 = now on active duty, 2 = active duty in the
past but not now, 3 = only active duty for training in Reserves/National Guard, 4 = never served).
'VPSP' code 01 
(verified in the data dictionary: 01 = Gulf War: 9/2001 or later (Post 9/11)).
Outcome `PERNP` is NA for people under 16, so those rows drop out too.
```{r filter-veterans}
vets <- pums_raw |>
  filter(MIL == "2", VPSP =="01", 
  !is.na(PERNP))
```

Convert numeric variables back from characters (from read_csv) and adjust income/earnings variables.
```{r}
vets <- vets |>
  mutate(across(c(AGEP, PERNP), as.numeric),
         ADJINC = as.numeric(ADJINC) / 1e6,
         PERNP_adj = PERNP * ADJINC,
         JWMNP = as.numeric(JWMNP),
         WKHP = as.numeric(WKHP),
         WKWN = as.numeric(WKWN))

glimpse(vets)
```
```{r}
# See example categorical breakdown for possible high proportion missing variables
vets |> count(SCIENGRLP)
vets |> count(PAOC)
vets |> count(JWMNP)
```
Check against criteria (i)-(v):
```{r criteria-check}
# (i) rows and predictor count -- you'll finalize predictors in Section 6
nrow(vets)

# (v) missingness overview across ALL columns (just to see what's usable)
vets |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "prop_na") |>
  filter(prop_na == 0)
vets |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "prop_na") |>
  filter(prop_na > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(prop_na))
```
## Impute NA with 0 for JWMNP, WKHP, WKWN by definition from Dictionary
```{r}
vets_filled <- vets |> 
  mutate(across(c(JWMNP, WKHP, WKWN), ~ replace_na(as.numeric(.x), 0)))
```

## 3(c) Remove duplicates

```{r dedupe}
# PUMS should be unique on SERIALNO + SPORDER; verify rather than assume
vets_filled |> get_dupes(SERIALNO, SPORDER) |> nrow()

n_before <- nrow(vets_filled)
vets_filled <- vets_filled |> distinct(SERIALNO, SPORDER, .keep_all = TRUE)
n_after <- nrow(vets_filled)
c(before = n_before, after = n_after)
```

**DONE:** confirm in text that duplicates were removed (even if zero found).

# 4. Holdout set

Split BEFORE any exploration or preprocessing. If you decided to keep one
person per household or to split by household, do that here.

```{r holdout-split}
set.seed(GLOBAL_SEED)

# Simple random 80/20 split of persons.
# NOTE: persons in the same household may land on both sides. Consider whether
# that leaks information (e.g., spouses with correlated incomes) and whether
# to split by SERIALNO instead (rsample::group_initial_split()).
split <- initial_split(vets_filled, prop = 0.80)

dev_raw     <- training(split)
holdout_raw <- testing(split)

c(total = nrow(vets_filled), development = nrow(dev_raw), holdout = nrow(holdout_raw))
```

Save the split. Store the holdout OUTSIDE the project directory so it cannot be
swept into AI tool context or your code zip.

```{r save-holdout}
holdout_path <- "/Users/gracekemmerenhendricks/Documents/Autumn 26/data/holdout/holdout_raw.rds"
dir.create(dirname(holdout_path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(holdout_raw, holdout_path)

dev_path <- "/Users/gracekemmerenhendricks/Documents/Autumn 26/data/dev/dev_raw.rds"
dir.create(dirname(dev_path), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(dev_raw, dev_path)

check_saved <- function(obj, path, label) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    cat("FAILED:", label, "not found at", path, "\n")
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }
  back <- readRDS(path)
  ok <- identical(obj, back)
  if (ok) {
    cat("OK:", label, "saved and verified --",
        nrow(back), "rows,", ncol(back), "columns, at", path, "\n")
  } else {
    cat("WARNING:", label, "exists but does not match the object in memory:", path, "\n")
  }
  rm(back)
  invisible(ok)
}

ok_holdout <- check_saved(holdout_raw, holdout_path, "holdout_raw.rds")
ok_dev     <- check_saved(dev_raw,     dev_path,     "dev_raw.rds")

# Safe-to-share record of the split (IDs only) -> can go in the code zip
dev_raw |>
  select(SERIALNO, SPORDER) |>
  write_csv("dev_ids.csv")
holdout_raw |>
  select(SERIALNO, SPORDER) |>
  write_csv("holdout_ids.csv")

holdout_csv <- file.path(dirname(holdout_path), "holdout_raw.csv")
dev_csv     <- file.path(dirname(dev_path),     "dev_raw.csv")

write_csv(holdout_raw, holdout_csv)
write_csv(dev_raw,     dev_csv)

file.exists(holdout_csv)   # TRUE
file.exists(dev_csv)       # TRUE

# Remove the holdout from this R session so nothing downstream can touch it
rm(holdout_raw, split, pums_raw, vets, vets_filled)
invisible(gc())
```
